newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium launches campaign against bad driving.
newsitem.headline: Belgium launches campaign against bad driving.

text.p: Belgium, with among the worst road accident records in Europe, on Monday launched a campaign against reckless driving.
Signposts will be placed at some of the main accident blackspots. The campaign is aimed primarily at cutting the number of children killed and injured on the roads each year.
Some 1,000 children are killed every year in traffic accidents, and a further 5,000 are injured.
"Jumping an orange light or a red light has become commonplace," Etienne Bauwens of the association for the parents of the victims of the road told RTBF television.
"The death of a child in a traffic accident has become unbelievably banal. You don't even mention it any more," he added.
He said car manufacturers were building into their models more and more protection for drivers, to the point where they think they are in little danger but forget the damage they can do to others.
Earlier this month European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock hit out at the poor standard of driving in Belgium.

"I consider it quite frankly to be an offence to the security and liberty of the human race," he told a news conference about the system that gives vehicles arriving from the right absolute priority over other road users.

According to the European Commission, Belgium comes seventh among EU nations in the league table of people killed per million cars registered, with 366 people killed in 1994 against Portugal's 1,043 and Sweden's 164.
